statement: The Linux and SDL HID consumers encode output effects under USB report 0x02 with the common block starting immediately after the report ID and BT report 0x31 with a three-byte Linux header (report ID, sequence/tag, tag). SDL uses two prefix bytes on BT (report ID, fixed marker) before its common effect block and appends a CRC; thus both put the common fields at USB absolute byte 1 and BT absolute byte 3 in Linux, but SDL places its effect fields at BT absolute byte 2. Treat the offsets as consumer-specific, not proof of interchangeable BT wrappers. Linux also supplies sequence/tag and CRC.

applicability.scope: Offsets are zero-based across full HID reports. Kernel and SDL have different Bluetooth wrappers; no physical packet capture.
